subject.title: Feature: Private Mode for demos and content creation

question: What exact privacy boundary should OpenClaw promise for Private Mode before implementation: context-only demo mode, or a hard per-session no-read/no-write/no-persistence mode?
rationale: The requested behavior changes a security and privacy promise across protocol, persistence, memory, plugin, tool, channel, logs, and UI semantics, so automation should not choose the threat model or public contract.

options.title: Hard per-session ephemeral contract
options.body: Add a session-level protocol and state marker that gates transcript/store writes, memory reads/writes, plugin persistence, channel defaults, and UI status; this best matches the issue and duplicate reports.

options.title: Context-only demo mode
options.body: Limit the feature to suppressing bootstrap/context injection and label it clearly as not private, no-persist, or memory-safe.

options.title: Defer for plugin/session API design
options.body: Keep the issue open while designing the plugin SDK and session lifecycle hooks needed for third-party persistence enforcement.

recommendation.title: Hard per-session ephemeral contract
recommendation.body: Add a session-level protocol and state marker that gates transcript/store writes, memory reads/writes, plugin persistence, channel defaults, and UI status; this best matches the issue and duplicate reports.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this as the canonical private-mode tracker and framed the product/security boundary questions that remain unresolved.
